Another critical parameter is the bed length, which directly influences the pressure drop across the sorbent layer. Table 9 shows that decreasing bed length (or thickness of the sorbent layer) leads to further reductions in pressure drop without noticeably affecting capture efficiency. These findings motivated additional optimization iterations to balance capture efficiency and pressure drop. The final optimized parameters for the 100 kg DAC sorbent bed are summarized in Table 10. As shown in Figure 35, a 2-minute evacuation to a vacuum pressure of 0.2 bar is sufficient to remove most of the nitrogen from the bed. During this evacuation phase, no heat is applied, only vacuum pressure is used. 37 Importantly, under these conditions, CO₂ desorption is minimal, indicating that the desorbed CO₂ can be cleanly diverted to the product stream afterward. Even at reduced vacuum levels, CO₂ recovery remains low, as illustrated in Figure 36. This negatively impacts product purity and highlights the need to apply heat to the bed to facilitate effective desorption. Figure 35.
